Emergency Spells break the Spell cadence but not the quality

title: Standby Spells are tiered by blast radius, trading per-use deployment cost against breadth of effect
content:
A.1.10.5.2.2.1 through A.1.10.5.2.2.4 organize Standby Spells into four tiers distinguished by scope and by deployment mechanics.

- **Single-collateral** (A.1.10.5.2.2.1): act on one collateral, and "for each instance of use, single-collateral Standby Spell contracts require a transaction to deploy the Standby Spell from a factory." Examples include SingleOsmStopSpell, SingleDdmDisableSpell and SingleLitePsmHaltFactory.
- **Grouped** (A.1.10.5.2.2.2): also factory-deployed per use, but "configured at the time of deployment with a specific list of collaterals," letting one spell cover several related collaterals.
- **Multi-collateral** (A.1.10.5.2.2.3): "are Spells in themselves and are thus reusable; beyond the initial deployment of the contract, no further deployment is needed" — they act across all collaterals.
- **Global** (A.1.10.5.2.2.4): also self-contained and reusable, but differ from multi-collateral in that they "operate on the Protocol globally and not on some set of collaterals" — e.g. SplitterStopSpell disabling the Smart Burn Engine.

The structural insight is that latency and precision are inversely arranged. The broadest actions are the fastest to fire, because a global or multi-collateral spell is standing and pre-deployed; the narrowest actions cost an extra deployment transaction at the moment of use.

That is a defensible ordering for a crisis: fine-grained intervention implies you have already diagnosed which collateral is at fault, which takes time you may not have, while the blunt instrument is the one you want available instantly. But it also creates a bias worth watching — under time pressure, the cheapest action to reach is the one with the largest blast radius.
description: Single-collateral and grouped spells must be deployed from a factory for each use; multi-collateral and global spells are Spells in themselves and are reusable without redeployment.
